verses.text: Then Job answered,
“How long will you torment me, and crush me with words?
You have reproached me ten times. You aren’t ashamed that you attack me.
If it is true that I have erred, my error remains with myself.
If indeed you will magnify yourselves against me, and plead against me my reproach;
know now that God has subverted me, and has surrounded me with his net.
“Behold, I cry out of wrong, but I am not heard. I cry for help, but there is no justice.
He has walled up my way so that I can’t pass, and has set darkness in my paths.
He has stripped me of my glory, and taken the crown from my head.
He has broken me down on every side, and I am gone. My hope he has plucked up like a tree.
He has also kindled his wrath against me. He counts me among his adversaries.
His troops come on together, build a siege ramp against me, and encamp around my tent.
“He has put my brothers far from me. My acquaintances are wholly estranged from me.
My relatives have gone away. My familiar friends have forgotten me.
Those who dwell in my house and my maids consider me a stranger. I am an alien in their sight.
I call to my servant, and he gives me no answer. I beg him with my mouth.
My breath is offensive to my wife. I am loathsome to the children of my own mother.
Even young children despise me. If I arise, they speak against me.
All my familiar friends abhor me. They whom I loved have turned against me.
My bones stick to my skin and to my flesh. I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.
“Have pity on me, have pity on me, you my friends; for the hand of God has touched me.
Why do you persecute me as God, and are not satisfied with my flesh?
“Oh that my words were now written! Oh that they were inscribed in a book!
That with an iron pen and lead they were engraved in the rock forever!
But as for me, I know that my Redeemer lives. In the end, he will stand upon the earth.
After my skin is destroyed, then in my flesh shall I see God,
Whom I, even I, shall see on my side. My eyes shall see, and not as a stranger. “My heart is consumed within me.
If you say, ‘How we will persecute him!’ because the root of the matter is found in me,
be afraid of the sword, for wrath brings the punishments of the sword, that you may know there is a judgment.”

footnotes.content: Job turns to speak directly—no longer silent under the weight. His answer will break open something true about suffering and the God who meets us there.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: How long? The cry of the afflicted—not a question seeking arithmetic, but a plea to be heard. Words are meant to build up; his friends' words have become hammers.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ten times they've accused him, circling like birds of prey. Yet they show no shame, no hesitation—cruelty cloaked in righteousness is the hardest to bear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: If I erred, the error is mine to carry. He speaks with dignity: even in collapse, a man can own his own mistakes and not live in others' judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yet you magnify yourselves against me—the friends play prosecutor and judge, swelling with the power of condemnation. Pride dressed as piety.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Here is Job's true confession: God has subverted him, surrounded him with a net. Not the friends' false accusation, but God's own hand. When we name the real adversary—when we look at the Almighty and say, 'This suffering comes from You'—we step toward truth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I cry out for wrong. I cry for help. But the heavens are silent—no voice, no justice. Many have known this silence. It is real, and it is part of the wages of living in a broken world.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He has walled up my way. Darkness crowds the path. When every door closes, when light leaves, the soul learns that it cannot save itself—and perhaps that is where faith must begin.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Stripped of glory, crown taken from his head—Job the prosperous, the respected, reduced to nothing. Emptiness is the only door through which humility can walk.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Broken down on every side, gone, his hope plucked up like a tree. There is no refuge in hope itself when hope is uprooted. Yet the fact that he speaks this means he has not yet lost his voice.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His wrath kindled, Job counted among God's adversaries. The sting is sharpest here: not that God is absent, but that He seems to be against him. Many faithful have touched this terror.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His troops come on together, build a siege ramp, encamp around my tent. The imagery is military, violent, total—not a tap on the shoulder but a siege. And yet Job reports it, which means some part of him stands outside it, seeing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Brothers far from him, acquaintances estranged. When suffering comes, people often vanish—not from cruelty alone, but from fear, from not knowing what to say. Isolation is suffering's long shadow.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Relatives gone away, familiar friends forgotten. The closer the bond, the sharper the abandonment. Yet he names each loss, refuses to pretend they did not matter.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Those in his own house treat him as a stranger, his maids as an alien. Home becomes unhome when it is populated by eyes that see you as other. This too is a death.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I call to my servant, he gives no answer. I beg with my mouth. Even servants, those bound by obligation, refuse him. Begging is humiliation—and it is also an act of will, the choice to cry out.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: My breath offensive to my wife, loathsome to my own mother's children. Those closest are most repelled. It is a terror beyond words, yet he speaks it aloud, refusing to swallow the shame alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even young children despise him and speak against him when he rises. Children are mirrors—they show us our own smallness without pretense. To be scorned by them is to be marked as less than human.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All my familiar friends abhor me. They whom I loved have turned against me. The reversal is complete: love becomes aversion, friendship becomes contempt. Yet naming it is the first truth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: My bones stick to my skin and flesh. I have escaped by the skin of my teeth. Physical dissolution is the sign—skin and bones alone, barely holding together. 'By the skin of my teeth' becomes an anchor phrase that later generations will inherit: survival by the thinnest margin, by grace alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Have pity on me, have pity on me, you my friends; for the hand of God has touched me. The repetition is a cry from the depths. He appeals to friendship, to pity—and frames his suffering as God's touch, not his own failure.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Why do you persecute me as God? His friends mimic God's harshness without God's wisdom. To pile onto the afflicted is to do the work of cruelty without the authority to speak.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Oh that my words were now written! He hungers to be heard, to have his testimony stand beyond the moment. To write is to refuse erasure—it is a claim that this suffering means something.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Inscribed in a book, engraved in the rock forever! Iron pen, lead, enduring stone—he wants his words to last, to become a monument. Writing is prayer, witness, and defiance all at once.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: But as for me, I know that my Redeemer lives. In the end, he will stand upon the earth. Here is the pivot—the moment when Job moves from complaint to confidence. His Redeemer (go'el, kinsman-avenger) lives; not doubt, but knowing. Generations of believers have heard in these words a witness to Christ.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: After my skin is destroyed, then in my flesh shall I see God. Death cannot end the meeting. To see God is to see the Judge who judges truly—and Job stakes everything on that encounter.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Whom I, even I, shall see on my side. Not as a stranger but as one known. My heart is consumed within me. Longing and terror together—he cannot hold the weight of this hope, yet he will not let it go.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: If you say, 'How we will persecute him!' because the root of the matter is found in me. Job turns back to his accusers with quiet assurance: there is a root here, and it matters. Not guilt, but truth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Be afraid of the sword, for wrath brings the punishments of the sword, that you may know there is a judgment. Readers today hear an echo: those who pile judgment on the suffering will answer. The Lord keeps His own accounts. In an age of easy condemnation, these words stand as warning that justice—true justice—belongs to God alone. As of 2026-10, we still need this reminder.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
